scientific_scope: Requirement-conditioned source screening for the frozen Materials Project Fe/Si phase-stability benchmark. Registry inclusion is not scientific admissibility and does not authorize target acquisition.

candidates.title: Open Quantum Materials Database v1.8 phase-stability data
notes: OQMD v1.8 is a February 2026 database release maintained by the Wolverton Research Group at Northwestern University and is distinct from the Materials Project source system.
OQMD data are licensed CC BY 4.0 and its REST API exposes stable entry identifiers, structures/compositions, formation energy delta_e, and stability as distance from the convex hull in eV/atom.
OQMD documents VASP 5.3.2, PBE-GGA, and VASP PAW-PBE potentials for its standard DFT calculations.

OQMD phase-diagram formation energies use fitted elemental-phase reference energies combined with DFT elemental energies and corrections associated with DFT+U treatment; this is not the same thermodynamic reference/correction convention as the frozen Materials Project summary energy_above_hull target.

Materials Project currently documents mixed GGA/GGA+U/r2SCAN thermodynamic processing and its own energy-correction/mixing schemes. Therefore a shared field meaning of distance above a convex hull and a shared eV/atom unit are insufficient for direct target equivalence.

Because thermodynamic_reference_state and energy_correction_semantics are confirmed mismatches, OQMD must not be acquired or fitted as direct source-disjoint external-validation evidence for this requirement. A separate cross-database diagnostic study could be scoped later without relabeling it as validation.

candidates.title: NIST JARVIS-DFT formation-energy and convex-hull data
notes: JARVIS-DFT is maintained by NIST and is a distinct source system from Materials Project; the live NIST site reports more than 77,000 JARVIS-DFT materials and identifies OptB88vdW formation energies as a core property family.

NIST documentation states that most JARVIS-DFT calculations use the OptB88vdW functional. The current JARVIS source code calculates formation energy using OptB88vdW elemental chemical potentials loaded from its own unary reference table and constructs convex hulls from those formation energies.

That OptB88vdW elemental-reference convention is not the frozen Materials Project GGA/GGA+U/r2SCAN thermodynamic mixing/correction convention. The difference is methodological, not a unit conversion, so direct target equivalence is rejected.

The current database does not expose a release identifier comparable to the pinned Materials Project database version in the evidence reviewed here, and the exact current-dataset VASP version, pseudopotential lineage, reuse terms for the data payload, competing-phase inventory, Fe/Si coverage, and cross-source structure mapping remain unresolved. Those gaps are not chased because confirmed target-method mismatches already block direct validation.

JARVIS remains valuable for a separately declared cross-functional or cross-database diagnostic study; it must not be fitted as direct external-validation evidence for the frozen Materials Project target.

Authoritative sources checked: https://jarvis.nist.gov/ ; https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/advanced-materials-design-electronic-and-functional-applications ; https://pages.nist.gov/jarvis/tutorials/ ; https://github.com/usnistgov/jarvis/blob/master/jarvis/analysis/thermodynamics/energetics.py ; https://docs.materialsproject.org/methodology/materials-methodology/thermodynamic-stability/thermodynamic-stability/gga-gga%2Bu-r2scan-mixing

candidates.title: AFLOW formation-enthalpy and convex-hull data
notes: AFLOW is maintained independently of Materials Project and exposes millions of material records, formation enthalpies, stable AUID identifiers, DFT metadata fields, and AFLOW-CHULL thermodynamic-stability tooling.

The official Aflux documentation states that data in the aflow.org repository are free for scientific, academic, and non-commercial purposes and prohibits other use. The current external-evidence requirement requires reusable evidence without that unresolved downstream restriction, so this candidate stops at the license gate.

AFLOW documents formation enthalpy per atom in eV/atom and multiple DFT/correction workflows, including CCE, but the exact thermodynamic target convention and Fe/Si cohort are intentionally not audited further after the hard reuse restriction is established.
This disposition concerns the present reusable external-validation contract, not the scientific quality of AFLOW or its suitability for academic diagnostic analyses.
Authoritative sources checked: https://aflow.org/documentation/ ; https://aflow.org/ ; https://aflow.org/publications/ ; https://aflow.org/aflow-documentation/index.html

candidates.title: Alexandria PBE convex-hull dataset
notes: Alexandria is an open independent project and its current site publishes versioned PBE convex-hull datasets, but the relevant PBE thermodynamic lineage is not source-disjoint from Materials Project.

The Alexandria dataset paper explicitly states that its PBE stability hull combined structures/data from AFLOW, Materials Project, and the authors' own group, selected calculations to match the Materials Project functional/pseudopotential/U settings, and applied Materials Project workflow corrections to the energies.

Because Materials Project data and correction lineage participate directly in construction of the source hull, this candidate cannot serve as independent external validation of the frozen Materials Project benchmark even if its target semantics are intentionally close to Materials Project.

Files/data for the published Alexandria PBEsol/SCAN release are CC BY 4.0, and the current Alexandria site exposes versioned PBE datasets and OPTIMADE endpoints. Reuse is not the blocker; source dependence is.

The correct disposition is diagnostic_only. Additional row-level Fe/Si coverage or structure mapping is unnecessary for deciding the current source-disjoint requirement and must not mask the already confirmed provenance dependence.

Authoritative sources checked: https://alexandria.icams.rub.de/ ; https://alexandria.icams.rub.de/datasets.html ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-022-01177-w ; https://archive.materialscloud.org/record/1755
